name: X-Hover Dining Table
subtitle: Parametric Hover-table variation
description: A 1:10 manipulation model of the 75-inch oak Hover table: a square-ended Bézier-rolled top, two sculpted closed end boxes, and independently selectable top and floor support layouts.

dimensionTargets: The image and supplied elevation establish a 75 in long by 35.5 in wide by 29.5 in high table envelope.
The tabletop has a flat rectangular plan, flat square end faces, and continuous Bézier-rolled long edges rather than rounded plan-view corners.
Exactly three blackened-steel C-channels run widthwise in flush underside mortises: one centered and two symmetrically derived between the end boxes, all clear of the rolled long edges.

The base contains exactly two closed transverse end boxes with independently selectable support layouts: an upper horizontal X or two original lengthwise stretchers, plus a floor X, one centered lengthwise board, or no floor connector.

Each end box has independently editable top and bottom values for both outer and inner corner radii, separately editable normalized Bézier tensions, rounded face edges, and a zero-spread default that can be adjusted to evaluate possible splay.
Every selected X crosses at the table center with a derived 50/50 half-lap and no overlapping solid volume; straight-support layouts contain no artificial lap.
Top and bottom support width, thickness, bearing-zone inset, and edge round-over contracts are independently editable while half-lap fit clearance applies only to selected Xs.
The selected upper supports bear directly against the tabletop underside and every selected lower support bears directly on the floor, with zero gap or spacer.

Exploded mode presents 14–16 assembly pieces according to the selected layouts: one profiled tabletop, three steel C-channels, four finished rail-and-stile bars per end box, two upper support members, and zero, one, or two lower support members.

Cut List mode presents the same selected pieces as six to nine grouped schedule lines with full-size finished dimensions, quantities, material, oak grain direction where applicable, exact constrained profiles, edge-treatment or C-channel section views, and joinery notes.
The default 1:10 manipulation model retains the full 75 × 35.5 × 29.5 in proportions.
invariants: Keep all full-size furniture dimensions independent from the mock-scale denominator.
Keep the tabletop end faces planar and square while changing only the two continuous long-edge profiles.

Keep exactly three widthwise C-channels flush with the tabletop underside; derive the center channel at table center and the outer pair symmetrically from the end-box inside faces, channel width, and editable clearance.
Keep every C-channel inside the tabletop, clear of both rolled long edges and both end boxes, with a positive U-section web and two positive flanges that fit within the tabletop thickness.

Keep the exposed C-channel webs and every selected upper-support top face on the same tabletop-underside plane, with no proud hardware and at least half of each support length retaining direct oak bearing for attachment.
Derive the end-box outer width from tabletop width and side overhang so width edits preserve the relationship.
Derive both inner openings from outer box dimensions and member widths; never scale the opening independently.
For each selected X, derive both diagonal lengths and equal-and-opposite plan angles from the end-box corner zones and keep the crossing at the table origin.

Derive each brace endpoint from the straight-rail tangent of the editable inner corner radius, inset the complete angled end face clear of that curve, and keep the support end planar and parallel with the end-box inside face; rail height controls vertical bearing overlap independently of support thickness.

Keep each selected X brace at full nominal width through the crossing, form complementary centered pockets at exactly half the nominal thickness, align every pocket boundary as a planar machining cut, and remove solid overlap between the two braces.
Round over only the bottom long edge of every selected support while keeping the top edge, end miters, and half-lap shoulders square.
Keep every selected top-support envelope coplanar with the tabletop underside and every selected floor-support envelope coplanar with the floor; expose no gap or spacer control.
Keep inner and outer corner curves as cubic Bézier functions whose control lengths equal radius times normalized tension.
Keep top and bottom exterior and interior corner radii independently editable because the observed curves are not concentric offsets.
Keep top and bottom support sections and edge radii independently editable; each selected support derives radius-aware placement and selected joinery from its own member contract.
Treat bottom spread as the explicit splay hypothesis; zero means orthogonal frame sides and remains the evidence-backed default.

Keep frame edge round-over below half the depth, side width, top-rail height, and bottom-rail height; keep the end-box side width independently editable down to 1/2 in because support members bear on the horizontal rails rather than setting the stile width.
Keep end boxes, their bottom spread, and all brace endpoints inside the tabletop width while preserving positive diagonal spans.

Derive the exploded rail, stile, tabletop, X-brace, stretcher, and center-board solids from the same Bézier, splay, round-over, contact-plane, and half-lap constraints used by the assembled model; do not substitute proxy blanks.

Keep exploded offsets presentation-only: parameter edits and layout changes must regenerate the selected 14–16 fully profiled wood and steel pieces without changing the assembled STL contract or resetting the camera.

Keep the cut list full-size and associative to the furniture parameters: changing mock scale must not change a listed fabrication dimension, while dimensional edits must update the schedule, exact SVG profile, section view, radii, tensions, round-overs, end cuts, and half-lap geometry.

Derive separate full-size top-rail, bottom-rail, and mirrored vertical-stile routing templates from the exact finished B1/B2/B3 part profiles used by the assembled, exploded, and cut-list modes; each asymmetric rail owns its Bézier corner returns and each stile runs only tangent-to-tangent.

Split all three routing templates by the editable usable square print-plate span, keep every STL flat and inside that envelope, and join adjacent pieces with complementary in-plane dovetails sized by explicit depth and fit-clearance controls.
Keep routing-template export at full furniture size and 1/8 in nominal thickness regardless of the manipulation-model scale; use the mock-scale denominator only for the on-screen template preview.
Label listed sizes as finished nominal dimensions and keep rough-milling allowance explicit rather than silently adding stock to any part.
Generate parallel upper lengthwise stretchers only when selected, generate exactly one centered floor board only when selected, and never generate hover pads or spacer blocks.

Expose a geometry-only wobble screen with independent racking, torsion, tipping, floor-rocking, and member-stiffness grades; keep its formulas transparent and never present it as structural certification.
Keep structural sensitivity monotonic: increasing overall height cannot improve the overall score, while increasing end-box side width or depth cannot reduce its racking score.
Treat oak grain and finish as renderer materials only; the STL geometry remains material-neutral.

scripts.name: audit
scripts.description: Validates the image-derived dimensions, end-box curves, selectable support layouts, conditional half-laps, zero-gap contacts, and procedural source contract.
